## Why This Exists

post/mod.rs::find_header_boundary() first scans for 

, then falls back to 

. The fallback scan can match 

 that appears as the LF parts of two consecutive CRLF lines: e.g. '...header

body' — the CRLF scan correctly finds position 8, but if CRLF scan fails (unusual) the LF scan would match at a different position.

More critically: for articles that use CRLF throughout, both scans run. If the CRLF separator search fails to find a match (e.g. article uses mixed endings), the LF fallback could match 

 that is actually inside the body (not at a true header boundary).

## Acceptance Criteria

Document the mixed-ending behaviour. Consider whether the LF fallback scan could be removed safely now that NNTP normalizes to CRLF before storage.
title: post/mod.rs::find_header_boundary: bare-LF scan can find separator inside CRLF body
